absent: No participatory action research lineage (Freire, Fals-Borda) and no Global South or decolonial sources; the theory base is Anglo-European public administration and STS.
forYou: Levin et al. (2012) on 'super wicked problems' argues for policies that constrain our future selves: constraint as a design tool, close to Juarrero's enabling constraints.
method: References from Crossref; strands and narrative by Claude, grounded only in the reference list and title.
narrative: The root is Rittel and Webber's 'Dilemmas in a general theory of planning' (1973). The paper follows its revival in policy studies (Head; Alford) and then steps into the 2019 Policy and Society debate that asked whether 'wickedness' had become an empty label.

Its move is to relocate the problem: dilemmas are not properties of problems but arise at boundaries between sectors. For that it borrows from science and technology studies (Gieryn's boundary-work, Star's boundary objects) and from paradox theory in organisation studies (Lewis; Vangen).
A less common layer is time and space: Barbara Adam's timescapes and Doreen Massey's relational space frame why cross-sector dilemmas persist.
